relations.note: Toci accompanies her son; her ixiptla’s thigh-skin becomes his ritual mask.
The maize god is explicitly called Cinteotl or Itztlacoliuhqui during Ochpaniztli.
His struck, face-covered frost form is reconstructed as Itztlacoliuhqui.
relations.source: Leyenda de los Soles; Sahaguntine frost passages

relations.note: As the Morning Star, he shoots and misses; Tonatiuh retaliates and strikes him.
Modern typology groups him with Tezcatlipoca through shared obsidian, punishment, fate, and obscured vision.
relations.source: Nicholson, Religion in Pre-Hispanic Central Mexico

relations.note: They appear in a shared sacrificial and obsidian configuration with disputed narrative meaning.
